understood that he had drawn north at the bottom, for
reasons of his own.

She laid her sheet beside his. Where hers showed water,
his showed a road lined with alder and a place called
Saint Bride’s Acre, with a small cross to mark a chapel.
Nobody in Low Harbor had heard of it. The harbormaster
said the dead were entitled to their opinions, and
poured the tea.

Three weeks later the water went down. They walked out
along the line of the drowned man’s road and found it
under a hand’s depth of silt, cobbled, running straight
toward nothing. The boy said camino, and then, because
she was paying him, road. At the end of it stood the
